title: Cut garbage collection to 2.4% of CPU on a fraud service
summary: I profiled a fraud-prevention service, found it spent about 17.7% of CPU on garbage collection, tuned the JVM to bring that to 2.4%, and showed the team the before-and-after evidence.
what_would_have_happened: More hosts to handle peak load, with CPU burned on non-business work.
the_call: Measure with the profiler before changing code or buying capacity.
what_i_did: Read the flame graphs, raised the heap size and moved to the G1 collector, then posted before-and-after charts to the team with notes on how to read them.
what_changed: Garbage collection dropped from about 17.7% to about 2.4% of CPU, and supported throughput rose about 20%.
